Body: Potential fix/workaround: I was running opencode in keyless mode (no login). All other free models worked, but deepseek-v4-flash-free kept failing with 'Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable.' I created a fresh API key from the OpenCode Zen dashboard, connected with that key instead of keyless mode, and everything works now. Suspect keyless/anonymous Zen requests get deprioritized or routed differently on the free DeepSeek lane.

ran into this and it claimed hundreds of gigs, here is what my clanker had to say:

The bug is confirmed, but you shouldn’t file a new issue: [OpenCode #37671](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/37671) already tracks this exact V2/headless-command regression. Your source trace would be a valuable comment there.

## Root-cause chain

1. [`@opencode-ai/cli@0.0.0-next-17444`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@opencode-ai/cli) was built from commit [`3a4c8cdf`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/3a4c8cdf9d3b27fc65ca2e7e38038949e201db7e) by [workflow run 17444](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/31801417737).

2. OpenCode intends to lazy-load its default handler in [`src/index.ts:16`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/3a4c8cdf9d3b27fc65ca2e7e38038949e201db7e/packages/cli/src/index.ts#L16-L18).

3. That handler imports the TUI and `UpdatePreflight` at module scope in [`default.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/3a4c8cdf9d3b27fc65ca2e7e38038949e201db7e/packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/default.ts#L1-L10). `UpdatePreflight` directly imports `@opentui/core` in [`update-preflight.tsx:4`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/3a4c8cdf9d3b27fc65ca2e7e38038949e201db7e/packages/cli/src/services/update-preflight.tsx#L1-L5).

4. OpenCode builds with Bun standalone compilation and `splitting: true` in [`build.ts:92`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/3a4c8cdf9d3b27fc65ca2e7e38038949e201db7e/packages/cli/script/build.ts#L92-L107). The resulting main startup chunk statically imports a shared chunk containing `@opentui/core`, so `--version` evaluates OpenTUI despite never dispatching the TUI handler.

5. The affected build actually uses OpenTUI **0.5.3**, not 0.4.5. OpenTUI resolves the embedded Darwin library at module initialization, then explicitly performs eager loading:

   - [`resolveNativeLibraryPath()`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/v0.5.3/packages/core/src/zig.ts#L174-L180)
   - [`dlopen()`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/v0.5.3/packages/core/src/zig.ts#L282-L291)
   - [“Try eager loading” block](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/v0.5.3/packages/core/src/zig.ts#L6242-L6245)
   - Native package embeds the dylib using `type: "file"` ([`build.ts:247`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/v0.5.3/packages/core/scripts/build.ts#L247-L251))

6. Bun materializes that embedded `$bunfs` dylib into `$TMPDIR` for `bun:ffi` and never reuses or removes it. A standalone two-module reproduction calling `dlopen()` and then `library.close()` still left the dylib behind. This is acknowledged in [Bun #29585](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/29585); the deduplication fix [Bun #29587](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/29587) remains open.

## Paste-ready comment for [OpenCode #37671](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/37671)

Confirmed on macOS arm64 with `@opencode-ai/cli@0.0.0-next-17444` / Bun 1.3.14. A single `TMPDIR=<empty-dir> opencode2 --version` leaves one 5,086,336-byte hidden dylib. Its SHA-256 is `554e892f…`, byte-for-byte identical to `@opentui/core-darwin-arm64@0.5.3/libopentui.dylib`.

Exact build provenance: [workflow run 17444](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/31801417737) built commit [`3a4c8cdf9d3b27fc65ca2e7e38038949e201db7e`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/3a4c8cdf9d3b27fc65ca2e7e38038949e201db7e).

Source trace: the CLI lazily declares the default handler, but that handler imports `UpdatePreflight`, which imports `@opentui/core`. With `Bun.build({ splitting: true, compile: ... })`, the generated main entry statically imports the shared OpenTUI chunk. Therefore `--version` evaluates OpenTUI before command dispatch. OpenTUI 0.5.3 then runs its top-level “Try eager loading” block, reaches `bun:ffi` `dlopen()` on the embedded `type: "file"` dylib, and triggers Bun’s known orphaned-extraction bug.

I investigated this independently on OpenCode with the official DeepSeek provider and found a concrete cause for the cache behavior in my setup.

In my case, this was **not caused by OpenCode failing to send `cache_control`**. The problem was a globally auto-loaded `opencode-agent-memory` plugin that injected a millisecond-precision timestamp near the beginning of the system prompt on every request:

```text
<memory_metadata>
- The current system date is: 2026-08-15T18:49:19.957Z
```

A few seconds later, the next request contained:

```text
<memory_metadata>
- The current system date is: 2026-08-15T18:49:23.275Z
```

I captured the actual outgoing `/chat/completions` JSON bodies and compared adjacent requests. The first differing content was this timestamp in the second system message. The tool definitions were identical.

Because DeepSeek prompt caching is prefix-based, the changing timestamp caused the reusable prefix to end before the conversation history. This exactly matched the observed symptom: cache reads stayed pinned around the static prompt size while uncached input kept growing.

For example, in a long failing session I observed cache reads plateauing around:

```text
11,008 cached tokens
```

while uncached input grew to hundreds of thousands of tokens.

I then performed controlled A/B tests:

1. Removing the memory plugin entirely restored normal cache growth.
2. Making the injected metadata stable restored append-only request construction.
3. With the stable-metadata patch, one test session produced:

```text
total_miss:    32,118
total_hit:    969,344
total_prompt: 1,001,462
cache hit rate: 96.79%
```

Later requests in that session were typically in the 98–99%+ cache-hit range.

The adjacent request comparison after the fix looked like:

```text
Identical message prefix: 6 messages (A=6, B=18)
Identical tool prefix: 14 tools (A=14, B=14)

FIRST JSON DIFFERENCE:
path: $.messages.<length>
```

So the previous request became a true prefix of the next request again.

The upstream plugin fix has now been merged here:

https://github.com/joshuadavidthomas/opencode-agent-memory/pull/20

One important detail: simply removing the plugin from the `plugin` array in `opencode.json` was not enough in my setup, because `~/.config/opencode/plugins/memory.ts` was auto-loaded from the local plugins directory. Moving that file/symlink out of the directory was necessary for the clean A/B test.

This may not explain every report in this issue, but for users who have `opencode-agent-memory` or another plugin that injects dynamic data near the start of the system prompt, it is worth checking the exact outgoing request bodies before attributing the behavior to DeepSeek cache support or `cache_control`.

> Anyone found a solution for this? It is driving me absolutely f'ing nuts.

**On resolving my issue, it does not appear to be the same as the original post. Apologies.**

Updating my terminal configuration, `$HOME/.config/foot/foot.ini`, fixed the issue for me.

On researching, I found references to the feature and default value as far back as 2022, so the feature is unlikely to be the root cause. It does, however, fix the problem.

Hopefully, other foot users will benefit.

```
# default value is 'yes' but breaks opencode v1.17.3+ mouse handling.
alternate-scroll-mode=no
```

Additional Windows `1.18.18` data point with an operational availability failure. This was measured read-only while OpenCode was running under OpenChamber `1.18.4`; no payloads, IDs, titles, or paths were inspected.

### Database

- File size: 2.016 GiB
- `PRAGMA quick_check`: `ok`
- `PRAGMA freelist_count`: `0`
- 26 sessions / 1,816 messages / 12,164 parts / 48,814 events
- `message.updated.1`: 1,596,501,940 bytes
- `info.summary.diffs` within those rows: 1,592,917,364 bytes (**99.8%**) across 1,792 rows
- `message.part.updated.1`: 388,949,497 bytes

### Per-message amplification

- Rank 1: 81 updates, 736.4 MiB total, 11.4 MiB maximum event/diff
- Rank 2: 140 updates, 257.1 MiB total, 3.5 MiB maximum event/diff
- Rank 3: 89 updates, 213.2 MiB total, 2.8 MiB maximum event/diff
- The two largest active session aggregates held 998.5 MiB and 761.2 MiB of event JSON.

This is the exact `summary.diffs` shape described here, despite the database containing only 26 sessions. It also occurred on a 61.7 GiB RAM / Ryzen 9 9950X3D machine, so adding hardware only delays the failure.

### Runtime symptom

With three concurrent busy sessions, `opencode serve` became unhealthy twice in about 90 minutes: the health endpoint failed repeatedly, proxy requests progressed from socket hangups to `ECONNREFUSED`, and the OpenChamber watchdog force-restarted the managed server after its threshold plus stale-busy grace. Every in-flight turn was interrupted. The first incident also coincided with a separate Node tool process reaching its default heap limit, but the second did not.

I disabled snapshot tracking for this repository as a local mitigation. That sacrifices OpenCode file undo/revert, but should remove nearly all of the measured `message.updated.1` payload in this workload.

The supervisor recovery/UX gap is reported separately as openchamber/openchamber#2943.

Superseded by #42831: the requested control plane is devbox-local Docker, with agents remaining outside workspace containers.

Confirming this on a second adapter, with the request body captured off the wire.

**Setup:** Qwen3.8-27B served locally by [oMLX](https://omlx.app) (Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages`), provider declared with `"npm": "@ai-sdk/anthropic"`, opencode `1.18.18`. I put a logging reverse proxy between opencode and the server to see the real body rather than infer it.

**Captured request body** (agent had `"temperature": 0.33, "top_p": 0.77` configured):

```json
{
  "model": "Qwen3.8-27B-oQ6e-mtp",
  "max_tokens": 32000,
  "top_p": 1,
  "stream": true,
  "tool_choice": { "type": "auto" }
}
```

`top_p: 1` comes from the substring match in `ProviderTransform.topP()` (`transform.ts:550`, `if (id.includes("qwen")) return 1`). Same as reported, so this is not specific to `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`.

Two things I ran into that might be worth folding into whatever opt-out lands:

**1. The documented workaround does not cover `temperature` for custom providers.** Setting `top_p` on the agent does win (`request.ts:127`), but `temperature` is gated:

```ts
temperature: input.model.capabilities.temperature
  ? (input.agent.temperature ?? ProviderTransform.temperature(input.model))
  : undefined,
```

and `capabilities.temperature` defaults to `false` for user-declared models (`provider.ts:1461`, `model.temperature ?? existingModel?.capabilities.temperature ?? false`). So for a locally-declared model, agent-level `temperature` is silently dropped unless the model entry also sets `"temperature": true`. That took a packet capture to find — a config-level no-op with no warning.

**2. `topK` has no user override at all.** Note the asymmetry at `request.ts:127-128`:

```ts
topP: input.agent.topP ?? ProviderTransform.topP(input.model),
topK: ProviderTransform.topK(input.model),
```

`AgentConfig` exposes `temperature` and `top_p` but not `top_k`, so when `ProviderTransform.topK()` does return a value there is no way to override it from config. It does not bite Qwen today (`topK()` returns `undefined` for it), but it would for any model matching the `minimax-m2` or `gemini` branches.

I appreciate this may interact with the v2 direction in `specs/v2/config.md` ("Do not retain dedicated agent `temperature` or `top_p` fields", with agent-local `options` carrying `body` overrides instead) — in which case an `options.body` passthrough would address all three at once. Happy to help test whichever shape you settle on.

Thanks for the duplicate check. This one is a distinct data point worth keeping: it isolates a **deterministic protocol-level difference** (HTTP/1.1 + SSE -> guaranteed 500; HTTP/2 + SSE -> 200, 100% reproducible in the same minute from the same machine/key/network), not intermittent unavailability.

Comparison with the referenced issues:
- #40480 (flash 500 while mimo works): that report shows non-streaming also 500s during the outage window (Aug 4). In my case non-streaming over HTTP/1.1 consistently returns 200 — the failure is specific to streaming. Related, but the trigger differs.
